questions.q: What happens when you run `docker compose up -d`?
options: It only starts containers that already exist, and errors if any are missing
Compose creates the network (if needed) and then creates and starts every service defined in compose.yaml, detached
It downloads Docker Desktop and installs the Compose plugin
It deletes any named volumes before starting fresh containers
questions.explain: `docker compose up` reads the whole file, creates the shared network, and creates/starts every service -- `-d` just means detached, the same meaning it has with `docker run`.

questions.q: In a compose.yaml service definition, what does the ports: value "8080:80" mean?
options: Container port 8080 maps to host port 80
Host port 8080 maps to container port 80, the same host:container syntax as docker run -p
It limits the container to 8080 requests per 80 seconds
It sets the container's memory limit to 8080 MB
questions.explain: Compose uses the identical host:container port syntax as `docker run -p` -- the left side is the host port, the right side is the container port.

questions.q: Why does the catalog-data volume survive after `docker compose down`?
options: Named volumes declared under the top-level volumes: key aren't removed by docker compose down unless you add -v
Compose down only ever removes networks, never containers
Volumes are automatically backed up to Docker Hub
catalog-data is actually a bind mount, which can never be removed
questions.explain: `docker compose down` removes containers and the network it created, but deliberately leaves named volumes in place unless you pass `-v` -- that's what keeps your data safe across restarts.

questions.q: What does a services: entry's key name, like catalog, become?
options: Nothing -- it's just a label with no functional effect
Both the container's identifier within the project and its hostname on the Compose network
The name of the Docker Hub registry it pulls from
The name of the host machine running Docker
questions.explain: Compose uses the service key both to name the container (prefixed with the project name) and as the hostname other services on the same network can reach it by.

questions.q: What does docker compose down remove, and what does it leave behind by default?
options: It removes everything including named volumes, with no way to keep them
It removes the containers and the network Compose created, but leaves named volumes in place
It removes only the network, leaving all containers running
It removes only images, leaving containers and networks untouched
questions.explain: By default, `docker compose down` tears down containers and the network, but named volumes persist until you explicitly add `-v`.
